summary: case-006 (b.cetin@aegean.edu): Escalate per Risk Gate at confidence 0.6. F1 reports a sign-in from unseen device PH-9900 while the usual device is LT-6002 (ATT&CK T1078). Password-spray allegations tied to 78.187.4.44 and 193.140.10.17 were rejected; both IPs show high volumes of successful MFA completions across many accounts and are treated as shared-egress background noise. Although the model step was degraded and proposed monitor, evidence policy requires escalation because F1 is the only unconfirmed signal.

risk.rationale: Case case-006 (b.cetin@aegean.edu): The only verified evidence is F1 (LIKELY 0.6), a sign-in from previously unseen device PH-9900 versus the account's usual device LT-6002 (T1078). The two password-spray-then-success claims are rejected: both IPs (78.187.4.44 and 193.140.10.17) are shared egress points with far more distinct accounts completing MFA than the threshold (186 and 208 respectively vs threshold 10), so the failures are background noise, not coordinated sprays. No confirmed account-takeover chain exists, there is no exposure, and there are no data-quality conflicts. The unexplained new-device logon is a weak signal insufficient for contain, not explained away enough for benign, and not conflicting/insufficient enough for escalate. Therefore: monitor.
